transcript.text: My Shark cordless battery got really hot on charge last night and this morning it looks puffed up, the plastic case has split at the seam a bit. Can I still use it till a new one comes? It's the IZ201UK.
AI service unavailable. Please try again in a moment.

Sorry, I think your reply didn't come through, it just said the service was unavailable. I'll ask again: can I keep using my Shark IZ201UK with this battery until a new one arrives? It's swollen with a split seam, there's a faint chemical smell this morning, and it's currently leaning against the kitchen cupboards next to the tea towels.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A swollen, very hot or chemical-smelling battery can catch fire. Stop using and charging it now, unplug the charger, and if it is safe to move put it somewhere non-flammable away from anything that could burn. Don't puncture, squeeze or try to open the battery, and don't put it in the household bin — take it to a battery recycling point. No, you must not use that battery again. A swollen battery with a split seam and chemical smell indicates internal failure and a serious fire risk; it could ignite at any moment. Please move the vacuum immediately to a safe, open area away from flammable items like your tea towels (ideally outside or in a garage if possible). Do not charge it, do not try to squeeze it back together, and do not throw it in the general rubbish bin. Take it to a local household waste recycling centre that accepts damaged lithium-ion batteries for safe disposal.

reading.symptom: swollen battery with a split seam and faint chemical smell

plan: They asked: "can I keep using my Shark IZ201UK with this battery until a new one arrives?" - answer that first.

Safety: a battery hazard is active. The fixed safety warning is shown separately, do not repeat it. It must not be used again until a qualified engineer has checked it: say that plainly. You may explain the likely cause and suggest checks that are safe with it switched off and unplugged, but never say or imply that a check could make it safe to use, or that they might not need an engineer.
Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Shark; model IZ201UK.
The fault they reported is: "swollen battery with a split seam and faint chemical smell". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the one or two safe checks, or the one question, that would best tell those causes apart. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
